title: Bimodule description of dg-category mapping spaces
statement:
Use the dg-category and quasi-equivalence conventions of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], the homotopy coherent localization conventions of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], and the nerves and spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; let $\mathsf{Hqe}$ be the ordinary localization at quasi-equivalences, and let $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{qe}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ denote the mapping space from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ in the homotopy coherent localization at quasi-equivalences. For dg categories $\mathcal C,\mathcal E$, the tensor $\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal E$ has object pairs and morphism complexes $\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal E(e,e')$, with composition using the graded symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{|x||y|}y\otimes x$. The opposite reverses morphism complexes and uses this symmetry in composition. Write $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ for cochain complexes with their usual complexes of graded maps. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$, and choose the cofibrant replacement $Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ of that node. Let $\mathcal W(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ have as objects dg functors $T:Q\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ whose restrictions $T(a,-)$ are cofibrant right $\mathcal B$-modules and are isomorphic in the derived category of right $\mathcal B$-modules to some representable $\mathcal B(-,b_a)$. A right module, its maps and its objectwise quasi-isomorphisms are as in [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution]; cofibrant here means lifting against all degreewise surjective objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of modules. Morphisms in $\mathcal W$ are only the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of bimodules. There is a natural equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{qe}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\simeq N\mathcal W(\mathcal A,\mathcal B),$$
where $N$ denotes the ordinary nerve, regarded up to weak homotopy equivalence. On connected components this identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ with isomorphism classes of all right quasi-representable $Q\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules in the localization at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms; the cofibrancy condition on the restrictions can be omitted for this isomorphism-class formulation. A strict dg functor $F:Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ corresponds to the bimodule $(a,b)\mapsto\mathcal B(b,F(a))$. These identifications commute with restriction in the first variable and derived extension of scalars in the second, meaning the left adjoint of restriction on localized module categories, computed by tensoring a projective replacement with the target category's morphism bimodule. If all morphism complexes of $\mathcal A$ are homotopically flat, the isomorphism-class bijection also holds using all right quasi-representable $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules in place of $Q\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules, with the comparison induced by restriction along $Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$; no fiberwise cofibrancy condition is imposed in this isomorphism-class formulation.

source.place: Section 4, Definition 4.1, Theorem 4.2, the remark before Corollary 4.8, and Corollary 4.8. Read online, absent from local literature. No Stacks tag supplies this dg-category theorem. For the flat-source variant, Section 3, Corollary 3.4 and the paragraph deriving tensor before Definition 4.1. For the homotopically flat-source formulation see also Keller, On differential graded categories, section 4.2, the definition of rep(A,B) immediately before Theorem 4.2.

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal C=Q\mathcal A$. Enlarge universes for the module categories; the model-structure node says this does not alter mapping spaces between the original small dg categories. Apply the projective module model structure in [lem-coef-dg-module-diagram-classification] to $\mathcal D=\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the full class of right quasi-representable modules, without a cofibrancy condition; this class is closed under quasi-isomorphisms in both directions. The representable $h_b=\mathcal B(-,b)$ is cofibrant: a map from it is determined by a closed element of degree zero at $b$, and such an element lifts across a surjective quasi-isomorphism by first lifting it and then correcting its differential using the acyclic kernel. More generally evaluation at the identity and $m\mapsto(f\mapsto m f)$ give inverse isomorphisms of complexes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(h_b,M)=M(b)$. Thus $h:\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ is fully faithful on actual Hom complexes.

For completeness, every cofibrant module $P$ is homotopically projective. A degree-$r$ cycle in $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,N)$ for acyclic $N$ is a chain map $P\to N[r]$. Here $N[r]^n=N^{n+r}$ has differential $(-1)^r d_N$ and the unchanged right action, so the cycle condition is exactly the chain-map equation. For any acyclic right module $L$, define $E^n=L^n\oplus L^{n-1}$ in every degree, with componentwise right action and $d(x,y)=(dx,x-dy)$. The projection $p(x,y)=x$ is a module map, degreewise surjective and a quasi-isomorphism since both $E$ and $L$ are acyclic. Indeed $h(x,y)=(y,0)$ is right-linear of degree $-1$ and $dh+hd=1$. Cofibrancy of $P$ lifts the chain map $f:P\to N[r]=L$ through $p:E\to L$. If $g$ is this lift, then $f=p(dh+hd)g=d_L(phg)+(phg)d_P$, proving it null-homotopic. In the unshifted Hom complex this says that $f$ is the boundary of $(-1)^rphg$, so every cycle is a boundary. The projective-resolution node now identifies $H^0$ of the Hom complexes on cofibrant modules with derived morphisms. Every object of $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ is therefore isomorphic in $H^0$ to some $h_b$, by its defining derived representability. Hence $h$ is a quasi-equivalence. This argument proves the Yoneda facts needed here directly, without using the downstream derived-enriched-Yoneda node.

source.place: Section 3, paragraphs after Proposition 3.5; enriched Yoneda and the quasi-equivalence into quasi-representable modules.

proof.text: Consider all right quasi-representable $\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules, with only quasi-isomorphisms as arrows; call this category $\mathcal V_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)$. The projective model structure exists by the diagram-classification node applied to the tensor dg category. Take a functorial projectively cofibrant replacement $RT\to T$ in this whole module category. Since $\mathcal C$ is cofibrant, its Hom complexes are projectively cofibrant; the evaluation clause of [lem-coef-dg-module-base-change] therefore says every fiber of $RT$ is cofibrant. The replacement is a quasi-isomorphism on every fiber, so $RT$ remains quasi-representable. Thus $R:\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$ is defined, and its replacement maps give natural transformations $iR\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal V}$ and $Ri\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal W}$, where $i$ is inclusion. A natural transformation yields a simplicial homotopy on nerves, so $N\mathcal W\to N\mathcal V$ is a weak equivalence. Notice that the proof does not assert cofibrancy is preserved by an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-coef-model-weak-equivalence-nerve], $\pi_0N\mathcal V$ is precisely the isomorphism classes of these objects in the module localization. This already justifies omission of fiber cofibrancy in the component formulation.

source.place: Section 4, remark immediately before Corollary 4.8, using Proposition 3.3 for cofibrant replacement of bimodules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-diagram-classification] with source $\mathcal C$, coefficient category right $\mathcal B$-modules, and the weak-equivalence-stable full class $\mathcal S$ from step 1. Its hypotheses hold: $\mathcal C$ is a small cofibrant dg category, the coefficient model structure is the stated projective one, and $\mathcal S$ is closed in both directions. Currying identifies strict dg functors $\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}})$ with $\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules, including their objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, by the tensor's Koszul interchange rule. Thus this node gives a bijection between $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S))$ and isomorphism classes of all right quasi-representable bimodules. The quasi-equivalence $h$ proved in step 1 becomes invertible in $\mathsf{Hqe}$, so postcomposition with $h$ identifies this Hom set with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal C,\mathcal B)$. The classifier sends a strict functor $F$ to its underlying diagram $hF$, which is exactly $(c,b)\mapsto\mathcal B(b,Fc)$. Together with step 2 this proves the required graph bijection on components, including all objects and their isomorphisms, rather than merely a pointwise assignment.

source.place: Section 4, Lemma 4.3 and Sublemmas 4.4-4.5; use the existing diagram-classification lemma (Section 6, Lemma 6.2) for precisely this component argument.

proof.text:
Choose a cosimplicial frame $\Gamma^\bullet\mathcal C$ with $\Gamma^0\mathcal C=\mathcal C$. Set $H(\mathcal B)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma^n\mathcal C,\mathcal B)$ and $V(\mathcal B)_{n,m}=N_m\mathcal W_{\Gamma^n\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)$. The frame lemma identifies $H(\mathcal B)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{qe}}(\mathcal C,\mathcal B)$. All $\Gamma^n\mathcal C$ are cofibrant, and all their cosimplicial operators and augmentations to $\mathcal C$ are quasi-equivalences, by the augmentation and two-out-of-three. Their Hom complexes are projectively cofibrant, so the tensor clause of the base-change node applies after tensoring with $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Restriction is consequently a Quillen equivalence on the corresponding module categories. It preserves and reflects the full quasi-representable classes: preservation follows by evaluating fibers; reflection follows because every object of the larger source is isomorphic in $H^0$ to an image object and a dg-module diagram carries such an isomorphism to a derived isomorphism of its values. The weak-equivalence-nerve lemma, and the replacement comparison of step 2 for each source, show that all outer operators of $V$ and the maps induced by $\Gamma^n\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ are weak equivalences on nerves. The bisimplicial diagonal lemma therefore gives a weak equivalence $\psi:N\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)\to\operatorname{diag}V(\mathcal B)$.

Define $\phi:H(\mathcal B)\to\operatorname{diag}V(\mathcal B)$ in degree $n$ by sending $F:\Gamma^n\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ to the constant $n$-simplex at its graph module. Its fibers are representables, which are cofibrant by step 1, so this really lies in $V_{n,n}$. Graph restriction is exactly precomposition, so the formula respects every simplicial operator. This construction does not yet claim $\phi$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Section 4, construction of phi and psi before Theorem 4.2 and the proof that psi is a weak equivalence.

proof.text:
Make the target naturality used below explicit. For $u:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$, extend each right-module value by $u_!$. It preserves cofibrant values and weak equivalences between them by the base-change node. It preserves the quasi-representable condition because its derived functor sends $h_b$ to $h_{u b}$. The canonical scalar-extension associators satisfy their unit and pentagon identities; the coend formula gives the canonical identification $u_!h_b=h_{u b}$. Thus graph construction is compatible with target extension, with those specified associators.

Here is the strict replacement, including both variables. Normalize extension along an identity target functor to be the identity, using the canonical coend unitor; hence source-only arrows act by literal restriction. Let $J=(\mathrm{dgCat}_{U})^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathrm{dgCat}_{U}$. At $j=(\mathcal D,\mathcal B)$ put $P(j)=\mathcal W_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal B)$, using the fiberwise definition of $\mathcal W$ also when $\mathcal D$ is not cofibrant. An arrow $a:j\to j'$ is a pair $(f:\mathcal D'\to\mathcal D,u:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E)$, and $P(a)T$ has values $u_!(T(f(d'),-))$. Source restriction and target extension commute by this value formula, so the scalar-extension associators make $P$ a pseudofunctor on $J$. Define $\widetilde P(j)$ to have families $T_a\in P(j')$ for every outgoing arrow $a:j\to j'$, together with isomorphisms $\gamma_{b,a}:P(b)T_a\to T_{ba}$ for every $b:j'\to j''$. Require the identity equation and the equation equating $\gamma_{c,ba}\circ P(c)(\gamma_{b,a})$ with $\gamma_{cb,a}$ after the canonical associator. Arrows are families of quasi-isomorphisms commuting with these equations. Evaluation at $a=\mathrm{id}_j$ is an equivalence of categories: its inverse sends $T$ to $(P(a)T)_a$, and the maps $\gamma_{a,\mathrm{id}_j}$ identify this family with the original family. Along $a_0:j\to j_1$ define $\widetilde P(a_0)$ by reindexing $a\mapsto aa_0$; reindexing composes strictly. Universes can be enlarged to contain $J$ and these families, by the model-structure node.

For a strict $F:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$, its graph family has value $h_{uFf}$ at $a=(f,u)$. The coend isomorphisms give its structure maps. Reindexing along $(f_0,u_0)$ gives exactly the graph family for $u_0Ff_0$, since at $(f,u)$ both values are $h_{uu_0Ff_0f}$. Hence the graph maps are strictly natural on $J$ after this replacement. Restricting the first variable to the diagram $n\mapsto\Gamma^n\mathcal C$ gives the strict bisimplicial graph diagram used in step 4; the augmentation gives its strict map from the constant-source diagram. The comparison with the original source diagrams can itself be made strict. Fix $\mathcal B$ and let $I$ be the source index category, including the augmentation. Both $P_i$ (source restriction only) and $\widetilde P_i$ are strict diagrams. Write $E_i:\widetilde P_i\to P_i$ for evaluation and $\kappa_a:P(a)E_i\xrightarrow{\sim}E_j\widetilde P(a)$ for the isomorphism $\gamma_{a,\mathrm{id}}$, for $a:i\to j$. At $i$ take the category of triples $(X,T,\epsilon)$ with $X\in\widetilde P_i$, $T\in P_i$, and an isomorphism $\epsilon:E_iX\to T$; a morphism is a pair commuting with $\epsilon$. Send this triple along $a$ to $(\widetilde P(a)X,P(a)T,P(a)(\epsilon)\kappa_a^{-1})$. The coherence equation for $\gamma$ makes this action strictly compositional. Both forgetful projections are strictly natural and objectwise equivalences: for the first projection an inverse at $i$ sends $X$ to $(X,E_iX,\mathrm{id})$, while the second uses the quasi-inverse of $E_i$. Thus their nerves give a zigzag of levelwise weak equivalences between the two bisimplicial diagrams. The diagonal lemma from step 4 makes their diagonals weakly equivalent. The graph lifts to this triple category by its canonical evaluation identification; under source restriction both entries become the graph of the composite, so this comparison also respects $\phi$ and the augmentation map $\psi$.

Use the strict target functor $G(\mathcal B)=N\widetilde P(\mathcal C,\mathcal B)$. Evaluation identifies its values with $N\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)$, and $\gamma$ identifies its arrows and composition homotopies with scalar extension. Retain the names $\phi,\psi$ for these strict family representatives; the bridge identifies them with the maps of step 4. They define $k=\psi^{-1}\phi:H\to G$ in the localized functor category, with the asserted source and target compatibilities.

source.place: Section 4, target extension pseudofunctor and its strictification, paragraphs between Lemma 4.3 and Sublemma 4.6. The split-family construction writes out the strictification rather than leaving it as an uncited standard fact.

proof.text:
Check the hypotheses of [lem-coef-model-finite-limit-detection] for this $k$. For $G$ use the evaluation identifications of step 5: the maps $\gamma$ identify the target maps and the specified composition homotopies, so homotopy-invariant assertions about the scalar-extension diagrams transfer to the strict family diagram. First $H$ sends quasi-equivalences to weak equivalences because it is the mapping-space functor from a fixed cofibrant source. It sends the terminal dg category to a point. For a strict pullback along a fibration in the target, degreewise Hom out of $\Gamma^n\mathcal C$ preserves the pullback, and the frame lemma makes the map on these Kan complexes a Kan fibration. The resulting strict pullback therefore represents the homotopy pullback.

For $G$, a target quasi-equivalence $u:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$ induces a Quillen equivalence on right-module categories by the base-change node. Its derived functors identify the quasi-representable classes: they send $h_b$ to $h_{u b}$; conversely essential surjectivity of $H^0u$ identifies each $h_e$ in the derived category with some $h_{u b}$. To apply this to whole $\mathcal C$-diagrams, $\mathcal C\otimes u^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasi-equivalence: each Hom map is a tensor of a quasi-isomorphism with a homotopically flat $\mathcal C(c,c')$, and essential surjectivity is witnessed by tensoring the isomorphisms with the identities of $\mathcal C$. Its extension is the fiberwise target extension, by the coend's Yoneda contraction in the unchanged $\mathcal C$ variable. For a fiberwise cofibrant $T$, the replacement map $RT\to T$ of step 2 is a quasi-isomorphism between cofibrant modules on each fiber. Therefore $u_!RT(c,-)\to u_!T(c,-)$ is a quasi-isomorphism on each fiber by the scalar-extension clause. This natural comparison identifies the actual target-extension functor on $\mathcal W$ with derived extension on its total projective replacements. The base-change and weak-equivalence-nerve lemmas now prove that $G$ sends target quasi-equivalences to weak equivalences. The pullback-descent node applies to our fixed cofibrant $\mathcal C$, so $G$ takes fibration pullbacks to homotopy pullbacks. At the terminal dg category, unitality forces every module value to be zero, since its identity morphism is zero. Hence $\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(*)$ has just the zero module and identity, and $G(*)$ is a point (also when $\mathcal C$ is empty). Finally, $\pi_0 k$ is the graph bijection of step 3: its degree-zero representative is $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B\mapsto h_F$, and the degree-zero component of $\psi$ is the identity. All hypotheses of detection are now verified, so $k$ is an objectwise weak equivalence. Since $\psi$ is a weak equivalence, so is $\phi$.

source.place: Section 4, conclusion of the proof of Theorem 4.2 using Sublemmas 4.6 and 4.7; each of the detection hypotheses is checked here.

proof.text: The zigzag $H(\mathcal B)\xrightarrow{\phi}\operatorname{diag}V(\mathcal B)\xleftarrow{\psi}N\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)$ consists of weak equivalences. Since $Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ is a quasi-equivalence, the frame comparison identifies its left end with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{qe}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$. This proves the asserted equivalence of spaces. Step 2 identifies the right-hand components with isomorphism classes of all quasi-representable $Q\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules; step 3 identifies the left-hand components with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ and fixes the graph normalization. Source restriction sends the graph of $F$ to the graph of its composite, directly from $(a,b)\mapsto\mathcal B(b,Fa)$. Target extension sends it to the graph of the target composite by the representable coend formula. The frame construction is natural in the homotopy theory of the source and target, and the strict replacement in step 5 respects both operations. Hence these equivalences and their component bijections have the naturality required in the statement. Target extension on arbitrary modules is its derived left adjoint, computed by a projectively cofibrant replacement and the same morphism-bimodule coend, exactly as stated.

source.place: Section 4, Theorem 4.2, functoriality paragraphs and Corollary 4.8.

proof.text: For the last assertion assume every $\mathcal A(a,a')$ is homotopically flat. The same holds for $Q\mathcal A$ by the model-structure node, so the tensor clause of the base-change node applies to $q:Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and gives a quasi-equivalence $q\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Restriction is therefore an equivalence of localized module categories, inverse to derived extension. Since $q$ is the identity on objects, restriction leaves every fiber right $\mathcal B$-module unchanged. It consequently preserves and reflects quasi-representability, and the inverse equivalence takes the same full subcategories onto one another: its unit and counit are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms after replacement and thus preserve this condition. It follows that restriction gives a bijection on their isomorphism classes. Combine it with step 7 to obtain the claimed classification by all $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules. No fiber cofibrancy was used in this comparison; it concerns all modules in their localizations.
